es: Comprender la idea principal, el lugar y una palabra regional en mensajes breves de hablantes de distintas variedades.

teaching.en: When you listen to an unfamiliar accent, focus on the gist first, because the topic and the place matter more than every single word.
teaching.es: Cuando escuchas un acento que no conoces, concéntrate primero en la idea general, porque el tema y el lugar importan más que cada palabra.
teaching.explanationEs: Gist = idea general; acento no familiar = unfamiliar accent.

because the topic and the place matter more than every single word.

teaching.en: The voice message was recorded on a noisy platform, so I could barely make out the words, although the place names helped me follow the topic.
teaching.es: El mensaje de voz se grabó en un andén ruidoso, así que apenas distinguía las palabras, aunque los nombres de lugar me ayudaron a seguir el tema.
teaching.explanationEs: Make out + palabras/voz = conseguir oír o entender con dificultad.
segments: The voice message was recorded on a noisy platform, so I could barely

teaching.en: An Australian friend invited us to a barbie, the local word for a barbecue, and warned that it would be the last one for a fortnight because the rain is coming.
teaching.es: Un amigo australiano nos invitó a una «barbie», la palabra local para barbacoa, y avisó de que sería la última durante dos semanas porque viene la lluvia.
teaching.explanationEs: Barbie (australiano) = barbecue; fortnight = dos semanas (RU, Irlanda y Australia).

that it would be the last one for a fortnight because the rain is coming.

teaching.en: In Houston, in the southern United States, a waiter asked whether y'all were ready to order, while my British friend quietly checked his mobile under the table.
teaching.es: En Houston, en el sur de EE. UU., un mesero preguntó si «y'all» estaban listos para pedir, mientras mi amigo británico miraba discretamente su celular bajo la mesa.
teaching.explanationEs: Y'all (sur de EE. UU.) = ustedes, un grupo; mobile = teléfono celular en inglés británico.
segments: In Houston, in the southern United States, a waiter asked whether y'all were ready
to order, while my British friend quietly checked his mobile under the table.

teaching.en: A Glasgow bloke thanked the driver with a quick cheers, and a regional word like that can reveal more about a speaker than an accent does.
teaching.es: Un tipo de Glasgow dio las gracias al conductor con un rápido «cheers», y una palabra regional así puede revelar más sobre alguien que su acento.
teaching.explanationEs: Bloke = hombre (RU y Australia); cheers = gracias o adiós informal (RU).
segments: A Glasgow bloke thanked the driver with a quick cheers, and a regional
word like that can reveal more about a speaker than an accent does.

teaching.en: To pick up on clues about where a speaker comes from, listen for regional words and for the speed and melody of the voice, not only the accent.
teaching.es: Para captar pistas sobre el origen de quien habla, escucha las palabras regionales y la velocidad y melodía de la voz, no solo el acento.
teaching.explanationEs: Pick up on = darse cuenta de algo sutil; las pistas son léxico, ritmo y entonación.

prompt.es: Según la transcripción, ¿qué palabra regional sitúa a Mia y qué significa?

choices.text: Y'all, which addresses a whole group in the southern United States.
Y'all, which is used in Australia to address a group of friends.
Y'all, which Americans use to address one person politely.

feedback.es: Y'all es la palabra regional de la transcripción: se dirige a un grupo y es típica del sur de EE. UU.; no es australiana ni se usa para una sola persona.

hint.es: Busca la palabra con la que Mia saluda a varias personas a la vez.

origin.text: Transcript: 'Hey y'all, it's Mia from Austin. The game starts at seven, so come early and bring a jacket, because the stadium gets cold after dark.'

prompt.es: Completa con la palabra británica informal: «Gracias, es muy amable.»

accepted: cheers

feedback.es: Cheers es la palabra informal británica para dar las gracias, también entre desconocidos.

hint.es: Es la palabra británica de la lista que sirve para agradecer.

origin.text: Tom held the door for an elderly woman at a London station. She smiled at him and said: '___, young man, that is very kind of you.'

answer.text: Sorry, what does that regional word mean

feedback.es: What does … mean es la estructura para pedir el significado; sorry suaviza la pregunta.

hint.es: Empieza por la disculpa y termina con el verbo mean.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Leo y elige qué plan propone.

choices.text: An afternoon barbecue that will be postponed if the weather turns.
An afternoon barbecue that moves indoors if the weather turns.
A formal dinner at which guests are expected to bring presents.

feedback.es: Leo organiza una barbacoa por la tarde y, si cambia el tiempo, la traslada dentro de casa: no la aplaza ni pide regalos.

origin.audio: Hi everyone, it's Leo from Brisbane. We are having a barbie this arvo, so bring your mates and something cold to drink. Dad says the weather will hold until about six, and then we move the party inside. Do not bring presents, mate, just come hungry. It has been a very long fortnight at work, and I really want a proper Saturday.

prompt.es: Escucha el mensaje de Sara y elige por qué se ríe el propietario.

choices.text: She did not know the name of the party where she had been.
She used a word that sounds rude in Ireland.
She answered about the music when he was asking about the atmosphere.

feedback.es: Sara respondió sobre la música porque no conocía craic; el propietario se ríe del malentendido, no de una grosería.

origin.audio: Hello from Dublin, it's Sara. I have been here for a fortnight and I am already losing my accent! Yesterday my landlord called his mate over to fix the heating, and afterwards he asked whether I had enjoyed the craic at the party. I had no idea what he meant, so I told him the music was great. He burst out laughing and explained that craic means the atmosphere, not the band.

prompt.es: Escucha de nuevo y elige qué actitud muestra Sara al contar la anécdota.

choices.text: She finds her mistake funny and is curious about local words.
She is embarrassed by the mix-up and would rather avoid such parties.
She is irritated that Irish speakers do not change their words for her.

feedback.es: Cuenta el malentendido con humor y aprendiendo una palabra nueva: no muestra vergüenza ni irritación.

origin.audio: Hello from Dublin, it's Sara. I have been here for a fortnight and I am already losing my accent! He burst out laughing and explained that craic means the atmosphere, not the band.

prompt.es: Completa: «Si captas la idea general, puedes preguntar los detalles después.»

accepted: gist

feedback.es: La idea general (gist) es lo primero que hay que captar; los detalles pueden aclararse después.

origin.text: Do not worry about understanding every word at the first listening. If you follow the ___, you can always ask for the details afterwards.

prompt.es: Lee la escena. ¿Qué explica la duda del visitante británico?

choices.text: He realises that y'all means only one person, so he answers for himself.
He wonders who y'all includes, because the word is new to him.
He does not recognise barbecue and waits for his wife to explain it.

feedback.es: Mira a su alrededor porque no sabe a quién se dirige y'all, una palabra nueva para él; después acepta por los dos.

origin.text: A British visitor in Texas is asked: 'Are y'all coming to the barbecue on Saturday?' He looks around, because only he and his wife are standing there, and then he laughs and says that they would love to come.

prompt.es: Lee la transcripción. ¿Qué pistas sitúan mejor al hablante en Australia?

choices.text: Mobile, because only Australians use it for a telephone.
Bloke, because no other variety of English has that word.
Arvo and barbie, which are typically Australian words.

feedback.es: Arvo y barbie son típicamente australianos; mobile y bloke también se usan en el Reino Unido, así que no bastan para situarlo.

origin.text: Transcript: 'Right, mate, I will ring you on your mobile this arvo. Bring a bloke from the office if you like, and please do not forget the barbie on Sunday.'

prompt.es: Completa: «La línea tenía tanto ruido que apenas podía distinguir lo que decía.»

feedback.es: Make out + lo que se dice significa distinguir algo con dificultad; barely subraya que casi no se oía.

origin.text: The line was so noisy that I could barely ___ out what she was saying, although I caught the name of the city.

prompt.es: Ordena: «Ella se dio cuenta de las palabras regionales de su mensaje.»

answer.text: She picked up on the regional words in his message

feedback.es: Pick up on + algo significa darse cuenta de un detalle sutil; aquí, las palabras regionales que delatan el origen del mensaje.
